# Site Leadership Coach: Synthetic pump fire, 2024

*Learning purposes: not a statutory document*

**Audience:** Plant and site leadership (T4)

**Incident:** Synthetic pump fire · 2024-03-20

## Bottom line

- Seals were bought locally without a specification for two years. [FND-0003]
- No check stopped an untested pump returning to service. [FND-0002]

## How the site set this up

Graph: 3 nodes, 3 links [FND-0001; FND-0002; FND-0003]

- L4 OR 2.2 Spares Programme Failure → L1 AB 1.1 Step Omitted (2 mentions)
- L3 SV 1.4 No Guidance Provided → L1 AB 1.1 Step Omitted (2 mentions)
- L4 OR 2.2 Spares Programme Failure → L3 SV 1.4 No Guidance Provided (1 mention)

### Pathway 1: spares to restart

Seals were bought locally without a specification [FND-0003]. Nothing in the return-to-service step asked for a test [FND-0002]. The pump restarted untested [FND-0001].

## Signals that reached leadership

- 2022-03 (24 months before): Local seal purchases begin *(weak signal)* [FND-0003; EVD-0003]
  - Received by: Plant manager (budget owner)
  - Response: None recorded

## Culture signals

Buying seals locally without a specification had become routine; the findings record no challenge to it [FND-0003].

## Decisions for the leadership team

### Spares specification

**Decision:** Require a specification for every critical-spares order [FND-0003]
- Options: All critical spares now; Rotating equipment first
- Trade-offs: Longer lead times against fewer unknown parts.
- Owner: Plant manager

**Indicator:** Critical spares bought to specification [FND-0003]
- Measure: % of critical-spares orders with a specification reference

## What leaders will do visibly

- [ ] Ask for the leak-test record at every pump walk-through. *(next 30 days)* [FND-0001]
